target_domain: AI-assisted organic chemistry for retrosynthesis prediction, reaction outcome prediction, and multi-step synthesis pathway planning, especially using graph learning, mechanism-aware representations, and data-efficient learning.
core_gap: Current methods do not provide a unified, mechanism-constrained, data-efficient, uncertainty-aware modeling framework that can generalize across reaction classes and jointly support feasible, selective, interpretable multi-step synthesis planning under scarce, noisy, and biased experimental data.
relations: molecules are represented as graphs whose atoms and bonds are transformed by reactions
permutation-invariant graph encoding makes molecular predictions independent of atom ordering
retrosynthesis decomposes a target molecule into feasible precursor sets
reaction prediction maps reactants, conditions, and catalysts to likely products and selectivity
chemical mechanisms constrain plausible bond changes and retrosynthetic disconnections
catalysts and reaction conditions influence feasibility, yield, and stereochemical outcome
literature reaction data provide training examples for learned transformation models
meta-learning transfers shared reaction features from known reactions to low-data new reactions
mechanism-aware representations improve data efficiency and chemical plausibility
pathway planning connects individual reaction predictions into multi-step synthetic routes
uncertainty and interpretability determine whether predictions can guide experimental decisions
bottlenecks: dependence on large, curated, positive-only reaction datasets
poor generalization to new reaction classes, catalysts, substrates, or selectivity regimes
difficulty predicting stereochemical selectivity and complex reaction outcomes
fragmentation of retrosynthesis, outcome prediction, yield prediction, condition recommendation, and route feasibility
incomplete mechanistic constraints leading to plausible but experimentally invalid routes
lack of calibrated uncertainty for proposed steps and routes
limited interpretability that chemists can verify and trust
noisy, biased, and incomplete experimental reporting
narrow domain-specific performance of data-efficient and few-shot models
absence of multi-objective optimization for cost, safety, sustainability, and scalability
unresolved_tensions: generic end-to-end learning versus chemically constrained mechanistic modeling
broad coverage across chemistry versus data efficiency in narrow low-data reaction families
predictive performance versus transparent causal interpretability
single-task reaction prediction versus unified synthesis planning
learned statistical correlation versus mechanistic causal reasoning
route generation speed versus experimental robustness and uncertainty calibration
use of successful literature data versus learning from missing, negative, or biased outcomes
desired_solution_properties: data-efficient and adaptable to few examples
generalizable across reaction classes and catalyst regimes
capable of predicting feasibility, product distribution, yield, selectivity, and conditions
integrated with multi-step retrosynthetic pathway planning
robust to noisy, incomplete, and biased reaction data
optimizes practical multi-objective route criteria such as cost, safety, step count, and sustainability
supports decision-making in early-stage reaction and drug development
possible_mechanism_types: reaction-center graph neural networks and graph transformation models
mechanistic constraint layers or rule-guided decoding
neuro-symbolic integration of chemical knowledge and learned models
meta-learning and few-shot adaptation over reaction tasks
multi-task learning across retrosynthesis, outcome prediction, yield, and selectivity
probabilistic modeling, ensembles, or conformal prediction for uncertainty quantification
causal or counterfactual representations of reaction behavior
search and planning algorithms for multi-step synthesis routes
active learning and closed-loop experimental optimization
